text:
Squawka called it the best scoring rate of Leon Draisaitl's career, at 31, and our numbers don't argue much. He has 14 goals and 31 points in 17 games, a four-game point streak, and Edmonton owns 62% of the five-on-five expected goals when he's out there.

The 14 goals are where we'd ease off. They came from 9.5 expected, a 22% shooting rate against 19% last season, and the Oilers have scored 14.9 goals more than their chances deserve with him on the ice. Draisaitl has always finished better than the league, so part of that sticks. Not all of it.

What needs no luck is the passing. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 14.5 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 99th percentile among forwards, and this year he ranks seventh in the league in wins added by his goals. Our projection lands near 48 goals, with a range from 39 to 58. The thing to watch is whether the even-strength goals keep coming once the percentages settle, because the power play will be there either way.
headline: Draisaitl at 31, better than ever
